options: A) Riverside Adventure Park — This park offers thrilling zip-lines and high-rope courses through the trees. It is perfect for those who love an adrenaline rush and want to test their physical limits in a beautiful outdoor setting.

B) The Historical Museum — Explore ancient artifacts and learn about the city's origins. The museum features interactive displays that are great for families with children who want to learn while having fun.

C) Coastal Art Gallery — Located right by the sea, this gallery showcases local artists' work. It is a quiet, peaceful place to spend an afternoon admiring paintings and photography inspired by the ocean.

D) Mountain Peak Trails — If you enjoy long walks and breathtaking views, this is the place for you. Remember to bring sturdy boots and plenty of water, as the climb to the summit can be quite challenging.

E) City Botanical Gardens — A tranquil escape in the middle of the city. Walk through exotic flower displays and relax by the central fountain. It is an ideal spot for anyone looking for a calm, relaxing day out.
F) Old Town Cooking School — Learn to prepare traditional local dishes in a friendly group environment. This is a hands-on experience where you get to eat what you make at the end of the class.

G) Science Discovery Centre — This centre is packed with experiments and technology demonstrations. It is highly recommended for teenagers interested in engineering and how things work in the modern world.
H) Lakeside Boat Rentals — Rent a small rowing boat or a pedal boat for an hour or two. It is a fun way to get out on the water and enjoy the sunshine with friends or family.

lesenParts.text:
Moving to a new city is often described as an exciting adventure, but for me, it felt more like a challenge I wasn't ready for. Last summer, my parents announced that we were moving from our quiet village to the bustling city of Manchester. I had lived in the same house for fourteen years, and the thought of leaving my friends and my favourite local park was devastating.

When we first arrived, the noise was the biggest shock. Unlike the peaceful nights I was used to, the city never seemed to sleep. There were sirens, traffic, and people talking at all hours. For the first two weeks, I barely left my room. I felt like an outsider looking in, convinced that I would never fit into this fast-paced environment. I spent most of my time messaging my old friends, feeling sorry for myself.

However, everything changed when I joined a local photography club. I had always enjoyed taking pictures, and I thought it might be a good way to get out of the house. On my first day, I met a girl named Sarah who was also new to the area. We started exploring the city together, looking for interesting buildings and street art to photograph. Through her eyes, I began to see the city differently. Instead of just seeing traffic and noise, I started to notice the beautiful architecture and the vibrant culture.

It has been six months now, and I can honestly say I don't regret the move. While I still miss my old friends, I have built a new life here. I have learned that moving isn't just about changing your address; it is about changing your perspective. You have to be willing to step outside your comfort zone to find the hidden gems in any new place. If you are facing a big move, my advice is to find a hobby or a group that shares your interests. It makes the world feel a lot smaller and much friendlier.

lesenParts.text: Last Saturday, I decided to visit the new food market in the town square. I had heard so many great things about the fresh produce and the friendly atmosphere. I bought a large bag of them, along with some local honey. After walking around for an hour, I started to feel hungry. (3) __________ There were so many delicious options, from spicy street food to sweet pastries. I finally chose a small stall that sold traditional vegetable pies. (4) __________ It was the best lunch I have had in a long time. Before leaving, I made sure to pick up some flowers for my kitchen table. Membership fees are very reasonable, and if you sign up before the end of the month, you will receive a discount of 15 percent on your first year. We also have a cafe on the ground floor where you can relax after your workout. We look forward to seeing you there!

horenParts.instruction: Listen and answer the questions in Part 4.
horenParts.transcript: Interviewer: Sarah, you've been blogging for five years now. What made you start? Sarah: I was working in an office and felt bored. I took a trip to Peru and realised I wanted to share my experiences. Interviewer: Was it hard to get started? Sarah: Yes, I didn't know anything about photography or writing for an audience. I had to learn everything from scratch. Interviewer: Many people think travel blogging is just a holiday. What do you say to them? Sarah: It's definitely not! I spend hours editing photos and researching locations. It's a full-time job. Interviewer: Do you ever get lonely? Sarah: Sometimes, but I meet so many interesting people on the road that it balances out. Interviewer: What is your favourite part of the job? Sarah: Seeing a place I've only read about in books. It's magical. Interviewer: Any advice for beginners? Sarah: Be yourself. Don't try to copy other bloggers. Authenticity is what people want to see.
